hook: HC: protective homes for victims only, not suspects
hook_b: HC: protective homes for victims only, not suspects
tldr: A bench of Acting Chief Justice P Sam Koshy and Justice Narsing Rao Nandikonda, ruling on NGO Prajwala's petition, said protective homes are for victims only and issued coordination directions to police, magistrates, legal services and welfare departments.

beats.what: The HC issued guidelines so trafficking victims are not housed with suspected organisers.
beats.why: Protective homes were being used in ways that mixed victims with alleged perpetrators, the petition argued.
beats.care: Departments must name contact officers and report on separate facilities and segregation protocols.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: TOI (Nov 19): the court said its directions supplement, and do not override, existing law.

cards.q: Will these guidelines change how rescued people are treated?

qs: How will authorities assess risk without labelling people on an accusation alone?

facts.t: Each department must file a first status report within *3 months*, without naming victims.

viz.l: What the court ordered, and when
viz.verdict: Departments must report progress for a year

steps.e: Initial status reports to home dept
Follow-up reports for a year; collectors' review meetings
State nodal officer via women safety wing

watch: Initial status reports due to the home department within three months.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: Telangana high court directs separate housing for trafficking victims, issues guidelines to all stakeholders

fact: Telangana HC says rescue homes must *never* hold suspected trafficking organisers
twist: The bench also said a case or prior accusation alone cannot brand someone a trafficker.
